questions.subject: Science
questions.question_text: An object is placed at a distance of 15 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. The nature and position of the image formed is:

options.text: Virtual and erect, formed behind the mirror
Real, inverted and magnified, at 30 cm in front of the mirror
Real, inverted and diminished, at 20 cm in front of the mirror
Virtual and diminished, at 5 cm behind the mirror

questions.answer_text: Option B: Real, inverted and magnified, formed at -30 cm (in front of mirror). Using mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u => 1/-10 = 1/v + 1/-15 => 1/v = 1/15 - 1/10 = -1/30 => v = -30 cm.
questions.explanation: When an object is placed between C and F of a concave mirror, a real, inverted and enlarged image is formed beyond C.

questions.explanation: Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm where glucose is broken down into pyruvate without requiring oxygen.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question_text: If a uniform cylindrical copper wire of resistance R is stretched uniformly such that its length doubles, what will be its new resistance?
questions.answer_text: Option B: 4 R. Since volume is constant (V = A × L), doubling length halves cross-sectional area (A' = A/2). Therefore R' = ρ(2L)/(A/2) = 4(ρL/A) = 4R.
questions.explanation: Resistance is directly proportional to length and inversely proportional to area of cross-section.

questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements labeled as Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Exposure of silver chloride to sunlight for a long duration turns grey.
Reason (R): Formation of silver by decomposition of silver chloride takes place in presence of light.
Select the correct option from the following:

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.answer_text: Option A: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion. Reaction: 2AgCl (s) --sunlight--> 2Ag (s) [grey] + Cl₂ (g).

questions.subject: Science
questions.question_text: Why is double circulation necessary in human beings? Explain briefly.
questions.answer_text: Double circulation ensures that oxygenated blood and deoxygenated blood remain strictly separated. This allows a highly efficient supply of oxygen to body cells, which is essential to meet the high energy demands needed for maintaining constant warm-blooded body temperature.
questions.explanation: Comprises pulmonary circulation and systemic circulation.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question_text:
An electric heater rated 1000 W operates 2 hours daily. Calculate:
(a) The energy consumed by it in 30 days in kilowatt-hours (kWh).
(b) The total cost of energy consumed if the rate is ₹ 6.50 per unit (kWh).
questions.answer_text:
(a) Power P = 1000 W = 1 kW. Daily time t = 2 h. Total hours in 30 days = 2 × 30 = 60 h.
Energy = P × t = 1 kW × 60 h = 60 kWh (units).
(b) Total Cost = 60 kWh × ₹ 6.50 = ₹ 390.00.
questions.explanation: Energy in kWh = (Power in Watts × hours) / 1000.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question_text: Differentiate between Roasting and Calcination with one balanced chemical equation for each process.
questions.answer_text:
1. Roasting: Process of heating sulfide ores strongly in the presence of excess air to convert them into metal oxides.
Example: 2ZnS + 3O₂ --heat--> 2ZnO + 2SO₂↑

2. Calcination: Process of heating carbonate or hydrated ores strongly in limited or absence of air to convert them into metal oxides.
Example: ZnCO₃ --heat--> ZnO + CO₂↑
questions.explanation: Roasting produces sulfur dioxide gas, whereas calcination yields carbon dioxide gas.

questions.answer_text:
1. Ray diagram showing incident ray entering prism at first surface, bending towards normal.
2. Emergent ray bending away from normal at second surface.
3. Labels required: Angle of prism (A), Angle of incidence (i), Angle of refraction (r), Angle of emergence (e), Angle of deviation (δ).
4. Dispersion spectrum labeled: Red (deviates least) at top, Violet (deviates most) at bottom (VIBGYOR).
questions.explanation: Different wavelengths travel with different speeds in glass; violet has the shortest wavelength and bends the most.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question_text:
(a) Draw a neat diagram of the human excretory system and label:
    (i) Kidney, (ii) Ureter, (iii) Urinary Bladder, (iv) Urethra.
(b) Describe the structural and functional unit of kidney (Nephron) and explain how urine is formed in the human body.
questions.answer_text:
(a) Well-labelled diagram showing bilateral kidneys, paired ureters connecting to urinary bladder and terminating at urethra.
(b) Structural & Functional Unit: Nephron.
Urine formation steps:
1. Ultrafiltration: Blood enters glomerulus under pressure through afferent arteriole. Glucose, amino acids, salts, urea and excess water filter into Bowman's capsule.
2. Selective Reabsorption: As filtrate passes along renal tubule, essential substances (all glucose, amino acids, major portion of salts and water) are reabsorbed back into peritubular capillaries.
3. Tubular Secretion: Extra potassium and hydrogen ions are secreted into tubule to maintain ionic balance.
The remaining fluid is urine, collected in collecting duct.
questions.explanation: Diagram carries 2 marks, mechanism of nephron and urine formation carries 3 marks.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question_text:
(a) What are homologous series of carbon compounds? State any two characteristics.
(b) An organic compound 'A' (C₂H₆O) on oxidation with alkaline KMnO₄ gives compound 'B'. Compound 'A' and 'B' react in presence of concentrated H₂SO₄ to form a sweet-smelling compound 'C'.
    (i) Identify compounds A, B, and C.
    (ii) Write the chemical equation for the formation of compound C and name the reaction.
questions.answer_text:
(a) Homologous Series: A group or family of organic compounds having the same functional group and similar chemical properties in which successive members differ by -CH₂- unit and 14 u in molecular mass.
Characteristics: (i) Common general formula. (ii) Gradual gradation in physical properties (boiling point increases with mass).

(b) Identification:
(i) Compound A: Ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH)
    Compound B: Ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH)
    Compound C: Ethyl ethanoate (CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ - sweet smelling ester)
(ii) Chemical Equation:
    CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH --(conc. H₂SO₄)--> CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O
    Reaction Name: Esterification reaction.
questions.explanation: Standard 5-mark organic chemistry question frequently appearing in Class 10 board exams.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question_text:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow:
Gregor Johann Mendel conducted hybridization experiments on garden peas (Pisum sativum) between 1856 and 1863. He studied seven pairs of contrasting traits. When he crossed pure breeding tall pea plants (TT) with pure breeding dwarf pea plants (tt), all F1 offspring were tall. Upon self-pollination of F1 plants, both tall and dwarf plants were obtained in F2 generation.

Questions:
1. What is the phenotypic ratio obtained in the F2 generation of a monohybrid cross? [1 Mark]
2. State the law of inheritance proposed by Mendel based on this monohybrid cross. [1 Mark]
3. (a) Work out the cross showing genotypes of parents, gametes, and F1 and F2 generations with Punnett square. [2 Marks]
   OR
   (b) If 800 pea plants are produced in the F2 generation, how many plants are expected to be pure homozygous tall? [2 Marks]
questions.answer_text:
1. Phenotypic ratio is 3 : 1 (3 Tall : 1 Dwarf).
2. Law of Segregation (Purity of gametes): Allele pairs separate or segregate during gamete formation, and randomly unite at fertilization.
3. (a) Parents: TT × tt -> Gametes: T, t -> F1: Tt (All Tall). F1 self cross: Tt × Tt -> F2 Genotypes: TT (1), Tt (2), tt (1) -> Genotypic ratio 1:2:1.
   OR
   (b) Pure homozygous tall plants (TT) constitute 1/4 (25%) of the F2 generation.
   Expected plants = 1/4 × 800 = 200 plants.
questions.explanation: Passage-based case study question carrying 4 marks as per latest CBSE pattern.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: If two positive integers a and b are written as a = x³y² and b = xy³, where x, y are prime numbers, then HCF(a, b) is:
questions.answer_text: Option B: xy². HCF is the product of the smallest power of each common prime factor involved in the numbers: min power of x is 1, min power of y is 2.
questions.explanation: HCF(a,b) = x^min(3,1) * y^min(2,3) = xy^2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: For what value of k does the quadratic equation 2x² + kx + 3 = 0 have two equal real roots?
questions.answer_text: Option A: ± 2√6. For equal roots, discriminant D = b² - 4ac = 0. Here k² - 4(2)(3) = 0 => k² - 24 = 0 => k = ±√24 = ±2√6.
questions.explanation: Standard discriminant condition D = 0.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Prove the trigonometric identity: (sin θ / (1 + cos θ)) + ((1 + cos θ) / sin θ) = 2 cosec θ.
questions.answer_text:
LHS = [sin²θ + (1 + cosθ)²] / [sinθ(1 + cosθ)]
    = [sin²θ + 1 + 2cosθ + cos²θ] / [sinθ(1 + cosθ)]
    = [(sin²θ + cos²θ) + 1 + 2cosθ] / [sinθ(1 + cosθ)]
    = [1 + 1 + 2cosθ] / [sinθ(1 + cosθ)]
    = [2 + 2cosθ] / [sinθ(1 + cosθ)]
    = 2(1 + cosθ) / [sinθ(1 + cosθ)]
    = 2 / sinθ = 2 cosecθ = RHS. Hence Proved.
questions.explanation: Using fundamental identity sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: State and prove Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales Theorem).
questions.answer_text:
Statement: If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio.

Proof:
Let ABC be a triangle and line DE || BC intersecting AB at D and AC at E.
Join BE and CD. Draw DM ⊥ AC and EN ⊥ AB.
Area(ΔADE) = 1/2 × AD × EN
Area(ΔBDE) = 1/2 × DB × EN
=> Area(ΔADE) / Area(ΔBDE) = AD / DB   --- (1)
Similarly,
Area(ΔADE) = 1/2 × AE × DM
Area(ΔDEC) = 1/2 × EC × DM
=> Area(ΔADE) / Area(ΔDEC) = AE / EC   --- (2)
Since ΔBDE and ΔDEC are on the same base DE and between the same parallels DE and BC:
Area(ΔBDE) = Area(ΔDEC)   --- (3)
From (1), (2), and (3):
AD / DB = AE / EC. Hence Proved.
questions.explanation: Compulsory theorem in CBSE Class 10 mathematics board examinations.

options.text: τ = p · E, U = p × E

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Define the term 'Mobility' of charge carriers in a metallic conductor. Write its SI unit.
questions.answer_text:
Mobility (μ) is defined as the magnitude of the drift velocity of charge carriers per unit applied electric field.
Formula: μ = |v_d| / E = qτ / m.
SI Unit: m² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ (or m²/(V·s)).
questions.explanation: Charge carrier mobility is independent of electric field for moderate fields.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
(a) State Huygens' principle of secondary wavelets.
(b) Using Huygens' wave theory, derive Snell's law of refraction for a plane wavefront incident on a plane refracting surface separating two media of refractive indices n₁ and n₂.
questions.answer_text:
(a) Huygens' Principle: (i) Every point on a given wavefront acts as a fresh source of new disturbance, called secondary wavelets, which spread out in all directions with the speed of the wave in that medium.
(ii) The forward envelope or tangential surface to these secondary wavelets at any subsequent instant gives the new wavefront.

(b) Derivation of Snell's Law:
Let AB be a plane wavefront incident at angle i on a plane refracting interface XY separating medium 1 (speed v₁) and medium 2 (speed v₂).
In the time τ taken by point B to reach C (BC = v₁τ), secondary wavelets from A travel distance v₂τ in medium 2 (AD = v₂τ).
From right-angled ΔABC: sin i = BC / AC = v₁τ / AC
From right-angled ΔADC: sin r = AD / AC = v₂τ / AC
Dividing both: sin i / sin r = (v₁τ) / (v₂τ) = v₁ / v₂
By definition, n₁ = c/v₁ and n₂ = c/v₂, so v₁/v₂ = n₂/n₁.
Therefore: n₁ sin i = n₂ sin r (Snell's Law of Refraction).
questions.explanation: Derivation carries 3 marks, principle carries 2 marks.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question_text:
(a) Draw a neat diagram of the human excretory system and label:
    (i) Kidney, (ii) Ureter, (iii) Urinary Bladder, (iv) Urethra.
(b) Describe the structural and functional unit of kidney (Nephron) and explain how urine is formed in the human body.
questions.answer_text:
(a) Well-labelled diagram showing bilateral kidneys, paired ureters connecting to urinary bladder and terminating at urethra.
(b) Structural & Functional Unit: Nephron.
Urine formation steps:
1. Ultrafiltration: Blood enters glomerulus under pressure through afferent arteriole. Glucose, amino acids, salts, urea and excess water filter into Bowman's capsule.
2. Selective Reabsorption: As filtrate passes along renal tubule, essential substances (all glucose, amino acids, major portion of salts and water) are reabsorbed back into peritubular capillaries.
3. Tubular Secretion: Extra potassium and hydrogen ions are secreted into tubule to maintain ionic balance.
The remaining fluid is urine, collected in collecting duct.
questions.explanation: Diagram carries 2 marks, mechanism of nephron and urine formation carries 3 marks.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question_text:
(a) What are homologous series of carbon compounds? State any two characteristics.
(b) An organic compound 'A' (C₂H₆O) on oxidation with alkaline KMnO₄ gives compound 'B'. Compound 'A' and 'B' react in presence of concentrated H₂SO₄ to form a sweet-smelling compound 'C'.
    (i) Identify compounds A, B, and C.
    (ii) Write the chemical equation for the formation of compound C and name the reaction.
questions.answer_text:
(a) Homologous Series: A group or family of organic compounds having the same functional group and similar chemical properties in which successive members differ by -CH₂- unit and 14 u in molecular mass.
Characteristics: (i) Common general formula. (ii) Gradual gradation in physical properties (boiling point increases with mass).

(b) Identification:
(i) Compound A: Ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH)
    Compound B: Ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH)
    Compound C: Ethyl ethanoate (CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ - sweet smelling ester)
(ii) Chemical Equation:
    CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH --(conc. H₂SO₄)--> CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O
    Reaction Name: Esterification reaction.
questions.explanation: Standard 5-mark organic chemistry question frequently appearing in Class 10 board exams.
